title_en: Zhao Shuhua v. Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. and Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over property damage compensation
ruling_gist_en: Fire safety concerns personal and property safety, and is a matter of public social interest. Ensuring the fire safety of buildings is a statutory obligation of the developer. Buyers under a commercial housing sales contract generally do not have the ability to inspect whether the purchased house complies with fire safety regulations, making it difficult to apply the rule of ordinary goods sales contracts that the buyer should inspect the quality of the product promptly after delivery of the subject matter.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over compensation for property damage; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Liaoning Province; Natural person; Legal person; Tort Liability Law; Property Management Regulations; Determination of fire safety obligations; Apportionment of tort liability for multiple causes leading to one result; Scope of supplementary liability of property management company; Partially upheld; Fire accident; Commercial housing sales; External wall insulation materials; Property management; Principle of fairness; Sales contract; Dispute over compensation for property damage of a limited company
full_text_en:
Zhao Shuhua v. Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. and Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd.

— Dispute over Compensation for Property Damage

【Ruling Summary】

Fire safety concerns personal and property safety and constitutes a public interest. Ensuring the fire safety of buildings is a statutory obligation of the developer. Purchasers in commercial housing sales contracts generally lack the ability to inspect whether the purchased property complies with fire safety regulations, making it difficult to apply the general rule in commodity sales contracts that the buyer shall timely inspect the quality of the subject matter after delivery.

Where multiple acts by the responsible parties at different times closely combine to cause a fire, and the tortious acts and causes of harm are sequential rather than cumulative, and the responsible parties each have gross negligence for the occurrence of the fire but without joint intent or joint negligence, they shall each bear corresponding liability. A developer who does not actively act to cause damage to the victim's rights and interests does not bear primary liability.

A property service enterprise has a statutory or contractual duty of safety prevention within the property management area and shall assist in preventing, stopping, or rescuing safety accidents and hazards. Where damage is caused by a third party, and the property service enterprise fails to exercise the care and attention of a professional manager, it shall bear corresponding supplementary liability to the extent that it could have foreseen and prevented the harm.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2018) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 206

Re-applicant (Plaintiff at first instance, Appellant at second instance): Zhao Shuhua, female, born on March 3, 1957, Han ethnicity, residing in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Chunguang, lawyer at Liaoning Guangjie Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance, Appellee at second instance): Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. (formerly Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.). Address: No. 390, Qingnian Street, Heping District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Legal representative: Zhu Lili, general manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xinhui, lawyer at Liaoning Tongfang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yanshan, lawyer at Liaoning Tongfang Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at first instance, Appellee at second instance): Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd. Address: No. 390, Qingnian Street, Heping District, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Legal representative: Guo Zhenghai, general manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xinhui, lawyer at Liaoning Tongfang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yanshan, lawyer at Liaoning Tongfang Law Firm.

Re-applicant Zhao Shuhua, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2015) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 00300 of the Liaoning High People's Court in the dispute with Respondents Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wanxin Company) and Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongyi Company) over compensation for property damage, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 4829 on December 20, 2017, granting a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to hear this case. Re-applicant Zhao Shuhua and her agent ad litem Jiang Chunguang, and the agents ad litem of Respondents Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company, Zhang Xinhui and Wang Yanshan, appeared in court. This case is now concluded.

Zhao Shuhua applied for retrial, requesting that the civil judgment (2013) Shen Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court and the civil judgment (2015) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 00300 of the Liaoning High People's Court be set aside, and that Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company be ordered to compensate Zhao Shuhua for losses caused by the fire: property loss of RMB 3,186,300, indoor property loss of RMB 2,199,363, rental expenses of RMB 357,000, deed tax of RMB 182,926.20, maintenance fund of RMB 8,646.56, property registration fee of RMB 5,000, overdue interest on the mortgage loan from Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. Shenyang Branch (hereinafter referred to as Industrial Bank) of RMB 100,000, and late payment penalty loss of RMB 228,000. Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company shall pay Zhao Shuhua insurance claim proceeds of RMB 2,000,000. Facts and Reasons: (1) The illegal use of combustible extruded polystyrene board as the exterior wall decoration material of the Wanxin Building was the direct cause of the fire in Block A of the Wanxin Building and its spread to Block B. 1. The "Fire Accident Determination" has determined that the cause of the three-dimensional combustion of the building involved was the ignition of the combustible extruded polystyrene board. 2. The "Interim Provisions on Fire Prevention for External Thermal Insulation Systems and Exterior Wall Decoration of Civil Buildings" (hereinafter referred to as the Interim Provisions), promulgated and implemented on September 25, 2009, stipulates that the combustion performance of insulation materials for buildings over 100 meters in height shall be Grade A. The Wanxin Building was completed and accepted on December 31, 2009, and passed fire safety acceptance on February 9, 2010. The Interim Provisions took effect before the acceptance, and Wanxin Company's use of combustible extruded polystyrene board in the exterior wall decoration of the Wanxin Building was illegal. (2) The insurance claim proceeds received by Wanxin Company after the fire are directly related to Zhao Shuhua's property loss. 1. The endorsement dated October 28, 2009, in the "Survey Report" included 226 properties in Block B of the building in the insurance coverage. The property purchased by Zhao Shuhua on December 29, 2009, had been included by Wanxin Company among the insured properties. 2. According to the "Insurance Claim Settlement Agreement," which provides: "In accordance with Article 5 of the Property All Risks Insurance Clause (2009 Version) of the People's Insurance Company of China, if during the insurance period, direct material damage or loss to the insured subject matter occurs due to natural disasters or accidents, the insurer shall be liable for compensation in accordance with the provisions of this insurance contract." The fire in question constitutes an insured event under the above insurance contract. (3) Zhongyi Company shall bear corresponding liability. The location where the hotel guest Li Xin set off fireworks was within the property management scope of Zhongyi Company and also within the security patrol scope of the building. As a property management company, Zhongyi Company allowed residents to set off fireworks indiscriminately in any area on New Year's Eve, leading to the fire. According to the relevant provisions of the "Regulations on Property Management of the People's Republic of China," Zhongyi Company shall bear management liability.

Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company argued: 1. At the time of the fire accident, the property in question had been delivered to Zhao Shuhua, and the risk of damage to the property had also transferred to Zhao Shuhua. The corresponding property loss should be borne by Zhao Shuhua herself. 2. Regarding whether the Interim Provisions apply to this case, Article 2 of the "Notice on Further Clarifying the Relevant Requirements for Fire Safety Supervision and Management of External Thermal Insulation Materials for Civil Buildings" provides that from March 15, 2011, all "construction project fire safety design review" and "fire safety acceptance filing projects" accepted by local authorities shall strictly comply with the requirements of this notice. The Wanxin Building passed the fire safety design review on April 3, 2008, before the Interim Provisions were issued. The acceptance time for Blocks A and C of the Wanxin Building was December 24, 2009, and the acceptance time for Block B was February 9, 2010, both before the implementation of the Interim Provisions. 3. Wanxin Company had no fault and should not bear liability for compensation. The fire accident determination found that the cause of the fire was the fireworks set off by Li Xin, who was the direct tortfeasor. The extruded polystyrene board used by Wanxin Company was tested as a qualified product, and there were no mandatory or restrictive provisions regarding other external insulation materials during the construction period of the building. At the same time, in October 2009, the Wanxin Building project passed the completion acceptance. Therefore, it cannot be determined that Wanxin Company was at fault. According to the basic principle of tort law, no fault means no liability, and Wanxin Company should not bear liability for compensation. 4. Zhao Shuhua's claim that the insurance claim proceeds received by Wanxin Company included Zhao Shuhua's property loss lacks factual basis. Buildings refer to unsold properties. The property in question had been sold to Zhao Shuhua before the insurance period and does not fall within the scope of the insurance policy. The insurance subject matter does not include any property in Block B. Furthermore, the policy mentioned by Zhao Shuhua in her appeal was a void policy, not the one used for claims after the accident. 5. The additional claims made by Zhao Shuhua that exceed the original trial claims should not be reviewed in the retrial. 6. Zhao Shuhua's claim that the fire in Block A of the Wanxin Building spread to Block B is inconsistent with the facts. In summary, the Respondent requested that the original judgment be upheld.

Zhao Shuhua filed a complaint at the court of first instance, requesting that Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company compensate for: property loss of RMB 4,573,155, indoor property loss of RMB 2,199,363, rental expenses of RMB 187,400, deed tax of RMB 182,926.20 incurred from the purchase of the property, maintenance fund of RMB 8,646.56, property registration fee of RMB 5,000, and loss of property appreciation of RMB 2,500,625. Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company shall bear the litigation costs of this case. Zhao Shuhua later added claims requesting that Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company compensate for overdue interest of RMB 100,000 on the bank loan for the purchase of the property and liquidated damages of RMB 228,000. During the trial, Zhao Shuhua also raised the argument that the insurance company's claim settlement to Wanxin Company after the fire included compensation for the property owners.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On December 29, 2009, Zhao Shuhua entered into a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Wanxin Company, agreeing to purchase two duplex apartments, Units 3407 and 3507 in Block B of the Wanxin Building, developed and constructed by Wanxin Company, with a total construction area of 200.05 square meters, for a total purchase price of RMB 4,573,155. After signing the contract, Zhao Shuhua paid Wanxin Company RMB 2,293,155 of the purchase price, and the remaining RMB 2,280,000 was paid through a mortgage loan from Industrial Bank. At approximately 0:15 a.m. on February 3, 2011, a fire broke out in the Wanxin Building, destroying the contents of Zhao Shuhua's property. The Shenyang Fire Bureau issued the "Fire Accident Determination" (Shen Gong Xiao Huo Ren Zi [2011] No. 0001), finding that the cause of the fire was that combination fireworks set off by Li Xin (a hotel guest in Block A) landed on the outdoor platform on the south side of Room 1109 on the 11th floor of Block B, igniting the plastic turf laid on the platform, which in turn ignited the exterior wall surface decorative insulation material. The cause of the disaster was that the exterior wall insulation of the Wanxin Building used combustible materials such as extruded polystyrene board, causing the fire to spread rapidly and form three-dimensional combustion.

Upon Zhao Shuhua's application, the court of first instance obtained fire archives from the Shenyang Fire Bureau. The archives recorded that after the fire, the Liaoning Provincial Building Materials Supervision and Inspection Institute tested five groups of samples from the Wanxin Building: molded polystyrene foam for thermal insulation, aluminum-plastic composite panels, plastic turf, silicone sealant, and extruded polystyrene foam for thermal insulation. The conclusion was that the molded polystyrene foam for thermal insulation, tested against the GB-2006 standard (Grade E), did not meet the standard requirements; tested against GB/T2406.2-2009 (top ignition method), the result did not meet the standard of Fs ≤ 150 within 20 seconds. The plastic turf, tested against the GB-2006 standard, did not meet the Df1 level requirements for combustion performance and was deemed non-conforming. The other three groups of samples were all qualified.

After the incident, the Heping District People's Court of Shenyang rendered a criminal judgment (2011) He Xing Chu Zi No. 1160, finding that the defendant Li Xin, while setting off fireworks and firecrackers, negligently caused a fire, resulting in significant damage to public and private property, constituting the crime of arson due to negligence. The defendant Li Xin was sentenced to three years' imprisonment for the crime of arson due to negligence. This criminal judgment has taken legal effect.

On July 10, 2008, the Shenyang Fire Bureau issued a review opinion on the construction project fire safety design to Wanxin Company, providing review comments on the interior decoration project of the Wanxin Building. On February 9, 2010, the Shenyang Public Security Fire Bureau issued an acceptance opinion on the construction project fire safety, stating that Block B (11th to 37th floors) of the Wanxin Building had been comprehensively evaluated and passed fire safety acceptance. Specific details: (1) The overall building layout, safety evacuation, and fire compartmentation basically met the original review requirements; (2) The indoor and outdoor fire hydrant system and automatic sprinkler system were tested, and water supply was normal; (3) The installation of safety evacuation signs basically met the standard requirements.

On September 25, 2009, the Ministry of Public Security and the former Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development jointly formulated the Interim Provisions, Article 2 of which stipulates that the combustion performance of external thermal insulation materials for civil buildings should preferably be Grade A and no lower than Grade B2. Article 4 stipulates that for residential buildings with a height of 100 meters or more, the combustion performance of the insulation materials should be Grade A.

In October 2009, Wanxin Company organized relevant units to conduct the completion acceptance of the Wanxin Building. On November 10, 2010, the Shenyang Urban and Rural Construction Committee issued a filing certificate for the completion acceptance of the Liaoning Province housing construction project, stating that upon review, the project met the requirements for completion acceptance filing and was filed.

After the fire, Wanxin Company negotiated with the Shenyang Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China, and the insurance company paid Wanxin Company a total insurance claim of RMB 476 million for the losses from this incident. Wanxin Company has since renovated the Wanxin Building.

The court of first instance rendered a judgment dismissing Zhao Shuhua's claims. The court of first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 79,400 was to be borne by Zhao Shuhua.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, Zhao Shuhua appealed, requesting that the original judgment be set aside and the case be retried or remanded, and that Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances.

The court of second instance found the facts: The second instance confirmed the basic facts found by the first instance. It further found that the "Survey Report" of Liaoning Zhengda Insurance Surveyors and Adjusters Co., Ltd. obtained by the court of first instance, at pages 22 to 26, under "IV. Insurance Policy Coverage," recorded that Policy No. PQYC200921010300000004 was accompanied by three endorsements, respectively amending the special agreements, the insurance address, and the insurance subject matter. One of the endorsements, EQYC201121010300000001, explicitly stated that effective from 0:00 on January 24, 2011, the insurance address was changed to No. 390A and No. 392, Qingnian Street, Heping District. The schedule of insured items under Policy No. PQYC201121010800000003 recorded that the insured subject matter 394 (B) had an area of 8,692 square meters, with a remark that Block B was a public area. The commercial housing sales contract between Zhao Shuhua and Wanxin Company included a delivery standard for "Huangchao Wanxin Hotel-Style Service Apartments," which specified that the interior base and decoration included: entrance door: solid wood steel door; ceiling: gypsum board ceiling, whitewashed and painted with latex paint... floor: imported natural stone/engineered wood flooring; interior walls: fabric-based wallpaper/finished wood veneer/finished soft package; kitchen system: electric ceramic stove, pull-out range hood, built-in microwave oven, built-in refrigerator; cabinet brand: Spanish brand Fagor; bathroom basin and toilet: German Duravit; faucet: German Grohe; bathtub: Jinkaideng; electric curtain track brand: Guangdong Lewu.

The court of second instance held that this case involved property damage to Zhao Shuhua's two properties and indoor property caused by the Wanxin Building fire, and Zhao Shuhua, as the holder of the rights to the above properties, sought joint compensation for property damage from Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company. Therefore, the focus of the dispute was whether Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company should bear liability for compensation for the property loss suffered by Zhao Shuhua due to the Wanxin Building fire.

(First, the property loss suffered by Zhao Shuhua due to the Wanxin Building fire should refer to the reduction in value of Zhao Shuhua's property caused by the fire, including direct and indirect losses. In this case, Zhao Shuhua claimed property losses mainly including: (1) Property loss and related deed tax, property maintenance fund, and property registration fee; (2) Indoor property loss; (3) Rental expenses for Zhao Shuhua's accommodation after the fire; (4) Loss of property appreciation of the property in question; (5) Interest and liquidated damages arising from Zhao Shuhua's overdue repayment of the bank loan; (6) The portion of insurance claim proceeds received by Wanxin Company related to the property in question. The second instance held: First, regarding the property loss and related expenses, the property price and the deed tax, maintenance fund, and registration fee paid by the buyer are necessary expenses for purchasing the property and can reflect the actual value of the property to a certain extent within a certain time frame. Although the property in question was damaged by the fire, the property itself did not cease to exist. Zhao Shuhua's claim for the actual loss based on the amount she spent on purchasing the property lacked factual basis. However, since the property in question was delivered with interior base and decoration items, the claim for property loss and related expenses should be based on the value of the interior base and decoration items as the loss. Second, regarding the interest and liquidated damages arising from Zhao Shuhua's overdue repayment of the bank loan, the loan taken by Zhao Shuhua from the bank to purchase the property in question, and whether she could fully perform her repayment obligations as a debtor, were not necessarily related to whether the property in question was affected by the fire. Moreover, the property list submitted unilaterally by Zhao Shuhua mainly consisted of indoor furniture, appliances, clothing, antiques, calligraphy and paintings, jewelry, and daily necessities, which was insufficient to demonstrate that the property damage caused by the fire affected her ability to repay. Therefore, there was a lack of causal link between Zhao Shuhua's claim and the Wanxin Building fire, and it should not be considered as part of her property loss. Third, regarding Zhao Shuhua's claim that the insurance claim proceeds received by Wanxin Company included the portion related to the property in question, Zhao Shuhua argued that Policy No. PQYC200921010300000004 was created before she entered into the commercial housing sales contract with Wanxin Company, thus the property in question had been included in Wanxin Company's insurance coverage. However, according to the Survey Report, the insurance policy and its three endorsements ultimately defined the insurance subject matter as the buildings and their ancillary equipment at No. 392, Qingnian Street, Heping District (Block A) and No. 390A (podiums), and did not include Block B where the property in question was located. Of the three policies taken out by Wanxin Company, Policy No. PQYC201121010800000003, which covered Block B of the Wanxin Building, had an insurance period starting after Zhao Shuhua purchased the property in question, and the schedule of insured items under that policy recorded that the insured subject matter "Block B was a public area." Zhao Shuhua's claim that Wanxin Company obtained insurance claim proceeds on account of the property in question lacked factual basis and should not be considered as part of Zhao Shuhua's property loss. As set forth above, the property loss caused to Zhao Shuhua by the fire should include indoor property loss, the value of interior base and decoration items, necessary rental expenses incurred by Zhao Shuhua after the fire, and the loss of property appreciation of the property in question resulting from the fire. As for other losses claimed by Zhao Shuhua, because they lacked a causal link with the Wanxin Building fire and had no factual or legal basis, the second instance court did not support Zhao Shuhua's above claims.)

Secondly, whether Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company were at fault for the fire at Wanxin Building. First, according to the fire accident determination issued by the Shenyang Fire Bureau and the criminal judgment of the Heping District People's Court of Shenyang (2011) He Xing Chu Zi No. 1160, the fire at Wanxin Building was caused by the discharge of fireworks by a third party, Li Xin, and the said criminal judgment has already determined that Li Xin's conduct constituted the crime of negligent arson, indicating that Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company did not directly commit the tortious act that caused the fire at Wanxin Building. Second, according to the fire protection archives of the Shenyang Fire Bureau retrieved by the court of first instance, the molded polystyrene foam for thermal insulation and the plastic lawn used in Wanxin Building failed to meet the requirements of Class E and Class Dfl, respectively. Therefore, it should be found that the construction materials used in Wanxin Building prior to the fire in this case did not comply with the relevant provisions of the Interim Provisions. However, the Interim Provisions were promulgated and implemented on September 25, 2009. Prior to this, China had not stipulated requirements for the fire performance of external wall insulation and decorative materials. As a departmental normative document, the Interim Provisions did not make special provisions regarding retroactive effect. Pursuant to Article 93 of the Legislation Law of the PRC: "Laws, administrative regulations, local regulations, autonomous regulations, separate regulations, and rules shall not be retroactive, except for special provisions made to better protect the rights and interests of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations." The aforementioned Interim Provisions have no retroactive effect. Prior to the promulgation and implementation of the Interim Provisions, the construction of Wanxin Building was substantially completed. The design and construction of Wanxin Building occurred before the promulgation and implementation of the Interim Provisions, and it ultimately passed the fire protection acceptance inspection by the Shenyang Public Security Fire Bureau and completed the record-filing procedures for completion acceptance. Therefore, the court of first instance's finding that "it cannot be determined that the use of extruded board and other materials on the outer wall of the building constituted fault" was not erroneous, and the court of second instance affirms this. Third, regarding whether Zhongyi Company was at fault for the fire at Wanxin Building. Article 37 of the Tort Law of the PRC (hereinafter the Tort Law) stipulates: "Where a manager of a public place such as a hotel, shopping mall, bank, or station, or an organizer of a mass activity, fails to fulfill the duty of security protection, causing damage to another person, it shall bear tort liability. Where damage is caused to another person by the conduct of a third party, the third party shall bear tort liability; if the manager or organizer fails to fulfill the duty of security protection, it shall bear corresponding supplementary liability." The fire at Wanxin Building was caused by the negligence of Li Xin, a third party. As a guest of Building A of Wanxin Building, Li Xin had no internal connection with Wanxin Company or Zhongyi Company. Zhao Shuhua's claim that the source of the fire was internal to Wanxin Building rather than external tortious conduct lacks factual basis and is not supported. The existing evidence also cannot prove that Zhongyi Company failed to fulfill the duty of security protection. Therefore, the court of first instance's refusal to support Zhao Shuhua's request for Zhongyi Company to bear joint and several liability was not erroneous. Finally, regarding Wanxin Company's voluntary repair of the property in question. After the fire at Wanxin Building, Wanxin Company carried out repairs, including on Building B of Wanxin Building, which contained the property in question. Wanxin Company's act of bearing the corresponding repair costs was its own disposition of its property, and it cannot be inferred from this that Wanxin Company should bear liability for property damage compensation for the fire at Wanxin Building. Zhao Shuhua's assertion in the appeal that Wanxin Company's repair conduct was actually fulfilling its compensation obligation lacks factual and legal basis.

In summary, Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company did not directly commit the tortious act that caused the fire at Wanxin Building, and the existing evidence cannot prove that Wanxin Company or Zhongyi Company were at fault for the fire. Therefore, Zhao Shuhua's request for a judgment ordering Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company to bear corresponding compensation liability for her property losses lacks factual and legal basis. The court of first instance's refusal to support this claim was not erroneous. Zhao Shuhua's grounds of appeal cannot be sustained and shall be dismissed. The judgment of first instance has clear factual findings and correct application of law, and shall be affirmed.

The court of second instance ruled: appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 81,696 shall be borne by Zhao Shuhua.

During the retrial, Zhao Shuhua submitted the following evidence to this court: Evidence 1: a house lease agreement and rent receipts, intended to prove that after the fire at Wanxin Building, Zhao Shuhua rented another house to live in, incurring cumulative rent expenses of RMB 357,000. Evidence 2: a civil judgment of the Heping District People's Court of Shenyang (2012) Shen He Min San Chu Zi No. 1025, intended to prove that Zhao Shuhua's indoor property and cash in the property were burned, rendering her unable to repay the housing loan. Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. sued Zhao Shuhua, and as a result, Zhao Shuhua paid an additional RMB 100,000 in overdue repayment interest and RMB 228,000 in liquidated damages. Evidence 3: an enforcement ruling of the Heping District People's Court of Shenyang (2014) Shen He Zhi Zi No. 00493, intended to prove that after the property in question was auctioned several times by the Heping District Court but failed, it was transferred at a low price of RMB 3,186,300 to Industrial Bank Co., Ltd., which had provided the mortgage loan, resulting in a loss of the purchase price for Zhao Shuhua. Evidence 4: a loss adjustment statement from page 73 of the appraisal report, the Wanxin insurance policy, and a project asset approval form, intended to prove that the insurance coverage in question included the property in Building B.

Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company argued in their cross-examination that the authenticity of Evidence 1 could not be determined and it was irrelevant to this case. They had no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 2 and Evidence 3, but they were irrelevant to this case. Evidence 4 could not prove that the property in question was within the insurance coverage.

This court finds, upon review, that Evidence 1 was entered into by Zhao Shuhua and a third party. Since the property in question was damaged by fire and could not be inhabited, Zhao Shuhua's rental of another house to live in was reasonable. Although Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company did not recognize the authenticity of this series of house lease agreements, they failed to provide contrary evidence to negate the reasonableness of Zhao Shuhua's rental. Regarding the rental loss claimed by Zhao Shuhua, the reasonable scope of the lease term and rent shall be determined comprehensively based on the series of house lease agreements and other evidence in this case. Evidence 2 and Evidence 3 are not objected to as to authenticity, and their probative content shall be determined in light of other basic facts of this case. Evidence 4 was evidence retrieved by the court of first instance and is not new evidence at the retrial stage.

Wanxin Company submitted the following evidence to this court: Evidence 1: a review opinion on construction engineering fire protection design from the Shenyang Fire Bureau (Shen Gong Xiao Shen Zi [2008] No. 31055), intended to prove that the construction design drawings of Wanxin Building passed statutory review, with the review passing date being April 3, 2008, before the promulgation and implementation of the Interim Provisions. Evidence 2: a review opinion on construction engineering fire protection design from the Shenyang Fire Bureau (Shen Gong Xiao Shen Zi [2008] No. 33141), intended to prove that the fire protection design drawings for the interior decoration of Wanxin Building passed review, with the review passing date being July 10, 2008, before the promulgation and implementation of the Interim Provisions. Evidence 3: a fire protection acceptance inspection opinion on construction engineering from the Shenyang Public Security Fire Bureau (Shen Gong Xiao Yan [2009] No. 11141), intended to prove that on December 24, 2009, Building C and Building A of Wanxin Building passed fire protection acceptance inspection, at which time the Interim Provisions had not yet been implemented. Evidence 4: a fire protection acceptance inspection opinion on construction engineering from the Shenyang Public Security Fire Bureau (Shen Gong Xiao Yan [2010] No. 076327), intended to prove that on February 9, 2010, Building B of Wanxin Building passed fire protection acceptance inspection, at which time the Interim Provisions had not yet been implemented. Evidence 5: a design calculation sheet for the external finishing works of the main building of Wanxin Building, intended to prove that the design basis for the external finishing works of the main building of Wanxin Building included the Code for Fire Protection Design of Buildings GB50016-2006 and the Code for Fire Protection Design of High-Rise Civil Buildings GB50015-95 (2005 Edition), which complied with the design code requirements in effect at that time. The Interim Provisions are not applicable to the external finishing works of the main building of Wanxin Building. Evidence 6: a completion drawing for the curtain wall works of the main building of Building B of Wanxin Building, intended to prove that the design basis for the curtain wall of the main building of Building B included the Code for Fire Protection Design of Buildings GB50016-2006 and the Code for Fire Protection Design of High-Rise Civil Buildings GB50015-95 (2005 Edition), which complied with the design code requirements in effect at that time. The Interim Provisions are not applicable to the main building curtain wall of Building B of Wanxin Building. Evidence 7, Evidence 8: inspection reports, intended to prove that the construction materials used in the curtain wall of Wanxin Building were tested and found to be qualified. Evidence 9: product certificates of conformity, intended to prove that the thermal insulation dry powder adhesive used in the curtain wall of Wanxin Building was qualified. Evidence 10: concealed works acceptance inspection record sheets; Evidence 11: construction decoration and finishing works completion acceptance inspection record sheets, intended to prove that the construction of the curtain walls of Building A and Building B of Wanxin Building, among other things, was confirmed by the construction unit, supervision unit, design unit, etc., to comply with the design and agreed standards. Evidence 12: an all-property insurance policy and endorsement, intended to prove that, effective from 00:00 on January 24, 2011, the insured property scope did not include the property in Building B of Wanxin Building. Evidence 13: the cover and an article from Issue 3, 2011 of F Huo Xian, intended to prove that when the fire occurred at Wanxin Building, the fire protection system of Wanxin Building was functioning well.

Zhao Shuhua stated in her cross-examination that she had no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 1 through Evidence 6 but objected to their relevance. At the time of the completion acceptance of Wanxin Building, the Interim Provisions had already been implemented, and Wanxin Company did not comply with these regulations. She had no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 7 through Evidence 11 but objected to their relevance. The completion acceptance did not conduct inspections in accordance with the Interim Provisions. She objected to the authenticity, legality, and relevance of Evidence 12. The appraisal report and insurance compensation agreement both stated that the insurance coverage of Wanxin Building included the property in Building B of Wanxin Building. She had no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 13 but objected to its relevance. The cause of the fire in this case was Wanxin Company's use of combustible extruded board, which led to Zhao Shuhua's property loss.

Zhongyi Company recognized the evidential views raised by Wanxin Company and had no objection to the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the above evidence submitted by Wanxin Company.

This court finds, upon review, that the Interim Provisions were promulgated and implemented on September 25, 2009, and Building B of Wanxin Building passed fire protection acceptance inspection on February 9, 2010, as already found in the original trial. Evidence 1 through Evidence 6 cannot prove that the Interim Provisions were not implemented at the time of the fire protection acceptance inspection for Building B of Wanxin Building and others. Evidence 7, Evidence 8, and Evidence 9 are test results for construction materials produced by the manufacturer, product certificates of conformity, etc. Evidence 10 through Evidence 11 are acceptance inspection sheets for concealed works and decoration works of Wanxin Building. The above evidence is not relevant to the disputed issues in this case. Evidence 12 is the insurance policy and endorsement for Wanxin Building. This court will determine its probative value in light of other basic facts of this case regarding the scope of coverage recorded in the policy and endorsement during the insurance period. As for Evidence 13, the article "Behind the Miracle: The N Weapons of 'Wanxin's Internal Skills'" from Issue 3, 2011 of F Huo Xian. This article contains a description of the operation of the sprinkler system at the time of the fire, stating that "under the sprinkler head, books were also unharmed," but it does not involve Rooms 3407 and 3507 in question. The on-site photographs of the affected property after the fire, submitted by Zhao Shuhua in the first instance, show that almost all furniture, appliances, and items inside the unit were burned to carbonization. Clearly, the description in the article "Behind the Miracle: The N Weapons of 'Wanxin's Internal Skills'" that the sprinkler system operated normally, furniture was intact, and there were water stain marks, among other things, is inconsistent with the actual situation, and this evidence is not admitted.

Zhongyi Company submitted the following evidence to this court: Evidence 1: a property service enterprise qualification certificate and a decision of the State Council on the third batch of cancellations of administrative licensing matters designated by the central government for local implementation, intended to prove that Zhongyi Company had property service qualifications and conducted annual inspections in accordance with regulations. After 2017, property service qualifications no longer required annual inspections. Evidence 2: one copy of the owner's occupancy document, intended to prove that, according to Article 4 of Chapter 2 of this occupancy document, the property service area was the interior space of the building with a construction area of 36,000 square meters, not including the exterior of the building. Evidence 3: a notice of inspection opinion on the completion acceptance of decoration works quality (Zhuang Zi [2012] No. 130), a notice of inspection opinion on the completion acceptance of decoration works quality (Zhuang Zi [2013] No. 015), and fire protection acceptance inspection opinions on construction engineering from the Shenyang Public Security Fire Bureau (Shen Gong Xiao Yan [2011] No. 1423, Shen Gong Xiao Yan [2012] No. 0127, Shen Gong Xiao Yan [2013] No. 0050), intended to prove that the decoration of the apartments in Building B of Wanxin Building was fully completed and passed acceptance inspection no later than March 4, 2013. Evidence 4: one copy of an engineering planning drawing and one copy of a construction layout receipt from the Shenyang Surveying and Mapping Research Institute, intended to prove that the three firework remnants found around Wanxin Building were not within the property management scope of Zhongyi Company.

Zhao Shuhua argued in cross-examination that she had no objection to Evidence 1. She had no objection to her own signature on Evidence 2, but it could not prove that the property service scope was limited to 36,000 square meters. She had no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 3 but objected to its relevance. Evidence 4 could not prove that the location where the third party discharged fireworks was not within the property management scope.

Wanxin Company raised no objection to the evidence presented by Zhongyi Company.

This court finds, upon review, that the parties to this case have no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 1, Evidence 2, Evidence 3, and Evidence 4. Evidence 2 and Evidence 4 cannot directly prove that the property service scope did not include the exterior of Wanxin Building.

Upon application by Zhongyi Company, this court, in the exercise of its authority, retrieved the criminal judgment of the Heping District of Shenyang (2011) He Xing Chu Zi No. 1160 (i.e., the criminal case of Li Xin for negligent arson, hereinafter the Li Xin Negligent Arson Case), the interview record of Liu Jiao by the Shenyang Fire Bureau, and the interview record of Ma Lichun by the Heping District Fire Brigade of Shenyang. The case file records that after the fire, the public security fire authorities interviewed relevant staff of Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company respectively. Ma Lichun, deputy manager of the procurement department of Wanxin Company, when interviewed on February 6, 2011, stated: "The 11th-floor platform of Building B of Wanxin Building was originally decorated with watercolor paintings, but the paintings later peeled, and owners reported it was unsightly. To decorate and beautify the platform, Wanxin Company laid a plastic lawn with a width of 1 meter and a length of approximately 40 meters in May 2010. The lawn was procured by him, and the supplier was a small company operated by a third-party individual." On February 8, 2011, Liu Jiao, a staff member of Zhongyi Company, stated in an interview: "The paintings on the 11th-floor platform of Building B of Wanxin Building originally cracked, and the construction unit replaced them with plastic lawn. The south-side platform was normally enclosed with glass, and neither the property company nor the owners could enter; only the construction unit could enter."

Zhao Shuhua argued in cross-examination that she had no objection to the authenticity, legality, and relevance.

Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company argued in cross-examination that they had no objection to the authenticity of the criminal judgment for Li Xin's negligent arson; regarding the laying of the lawn, Liu Jiao and Ma Lichun held a misunderstanding, as the lawn was actually laid by Zhongyi Company.

This court finds, upon review, that the criminal judgment (2011) He Xing Chu Zi No. 1160 has taken legal effect and can be used as a basis for determining the relevant facts of this case. The interview records in question were formed before this lawsuit occurred, that is, they were obtained through investigation and evidence collection by the public security fire authorities shortly after the fire in the Li Xin Negligent Arson Case. Ma Lichun provided detailed statements on the details of the purchase and laying of the plastic lawn, and the testimony of Liu Jiao can provide supplementary corroboration, thus having high credibility. The written statements and other documentary evidence submitted by Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company during the retrial stage of this case, from Liu Jiao and Ma Lichun, among others, are insufficient to overturn their prior statements. This court does not accept the claim of Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company that the flammable plastic lawn was laid by Zhongyi Company.

During the retrial, it was found that the notice of industrial and commercial change registration submitted by Wanxin Company to this court proves that Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. changed its name to Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. on May 19, 2017.

According to the investigation and inquiry by the public security fire authorities, the plastic lawn in question was laid by Wanxin Company.

Article 17, Paragraph 2 of the Commercial Housing Sales Contract (Contract No. GF-2000-0171) entered into between Zhao Shuhua and Wanxin Company stipulates that the right to use the external wall surface of the building where the commercial housing is located shall be owned by the seller.

Zhongyi Company submitted the Provisional Covenant for Owners of Huangchao Wanxin International Building (Apartments) in this case, which contains provisions on the rights and obligations of owners and the property company.

This court finds upon retrial that the disputed issues in this case are: 1. Whether Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company should bear tort liability for compensation for the property losses caused to Zhao Shuhua by the fire; 2. If they are liable, how the scope of tort liability to be borne by Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company should be determined; 3. How the scope of Zhao Shuhua's property losses should be determined.

I. Whether Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company should bear tort liability for compensation for the property losses caused to Zhao Shuhua by the fire

The original trial found that on February 3, 2011, a fire broke out at Wanxin Building, burning the items inside the property purchased by Zhao Shuhua. Zhao Shuhua requested Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company to compensate for the property losses she suffered as a result. The parties to this case have no dispute over the fact that the fire at Wanxin Building caused Zhao Shuhua's property losses. Based on Zhao Shuhua's claims and reasons, the nature of the dispute in this case is a tort liability dispute.

(A) Wanxin Company shall bear tort liability

The original trial found that the Shenyang Fire Bureau issued the Fire Accident Determination (Shen Gong Xiao Huo Ren Zi [2011] No. 0001) regarding the fire at Wanxin Building, identifying the cause of the fire accident as: "The fire at Wanxin Building originated from combination fireworks discharged by Li Xin (a guest staying in Building A) landing on the south-side outdoor platform outside Room 1109 on the 11th floor of Building B, igniting the plastic lawn laid on the platform, causing the external wall surface decorative insulation material to burn. The cause of the fire's development was: because the external wall insulation of Wanxin Building used combustible materials such as extruded board, the fire spread rapidly after ignition, forming a three-dimensional combustion." After the fire, the Shenyang Fire Bureau commissioned the Liaoning Provincial Building Materials Supervision and Inspection Institute to test the combustion performance of samples of the plastic lawn ignited by Li Xin's fireworks and the external wall insulation material of Building B of Wanxin Building. The conclusion was: "Tested according to the GB8624-2006 standard, the plastic lawn sample did not meet DF1 level requirements, and the test conclusion was unqualified; for the extruded polystyrene foam for thermal insulation, according to the GB8624-2006 standard (Class E), the sample met the standard requirements." The above evidence can be used as a basis for determining the facts of this case. Wanxin Company was the layer of the plastic lawn and the constructor/installer of the external wall insulation material. The use of these two non-flame-retardant materials was the main cause of the ignition at Wanxin Building, the spread of the fire, and ultimately the major fire accident. Wanxin Company was at fault and should be identified as a responsible person related to the fire accident.

1.  Wanxin Company was at fault for causing the fire. Based on the fire accident determination report involved in the case and the conclusion of the inspection report from the Liaoning Provincial Building Materials Supervision and Inspection Institute, it is sufficient to determine that the plastic lawn with substandard combustion performance laid on the southern platform of the 11th floor of Block B of the Wanxin Building was ignited after being splashed by the combination fireworks set off by Li Xin, which was one of the causes of the fire accident at the Wanxin Building. In this regard, Wanxin Company, as the layer of the plastic lawn, was at fault and bore corresponding management responsibility. When Wanxin Company was questioned by this Court, it stated that the fire involved occurred on New Year's Eve, and there were other residents setting off fireworks and firecrackers around the Wanxin Building. Therefore, the flammable plastic lawn laid by Wanxin Company clearly posed a fire safety hazard. According to common knowledge and life experience, it should have been foreseeable that residents following customs would concentrate on setting off fireworks and firecrackers on New Year's Eve, which might ignite the flammable plastic lawn. However, Wanxin Company did not take corresponding measures to eliminate the hazard for the above flammable materials, directly leading to the occurrence of the fire, which was obviously subjectively at fault.

2.  Wanxin Company was at fault for the spread and expansion of the fire, ultimately resulting in a major fire accident. Article 9 of the Fire Protection Law of the PRC stipulates, "The fire protection design and construction of construction projects must comply with the national engineering construction fire protection technical standards. The construction, design, construction, and engineering supervision units shall be responsible for the quality of the fire protection design and construction of the construction project according to law." Fire safety concerns the personal and property safety of citizens and belongs to the public interest. Ensuring the fire safety of a building is a legal obligation of the construction unit. The construction unit's declaration of approval for fire protection subcontracting in accordance with the law does not necessarily exempt it from civil tort liability arising from damage caused by fire safety accidents.

In this case, according to the facts found by the original trial, the external wall insulation material used in Block B of the Wanxin Building, where the house involved was located, had a combustion performance rating of E, which did not comply with the mandatory standard that the combustion performance of external wall insulation materials for such high-rise buildings should be Class A under the Interim Provisions. Wanxin Company argued that the Interim Provisions had not yet been issued when the Wanxin Building was designed and constructed, and the Wanxin Building had passed fire protection design review, completion acceptance, and fire acceptance, so it was not at fault. The above defense grounds cannot be established. First, from the contents of the "Opinion on the Fire Protection Design Review of the Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Building Construction Project" and the "Opinion on the Fire Protection Acceptance of Construction Projects," the Shenyang Fire Bureau's design review and fire acceptance of the Wanxin Building did not involve the fire performance of the external wall insulation building materials. Therefore, the Wanxin Building passing the fire protection design review and fire acceptance cannot prove that the external wall insulation materials used in the Wanxin Building met fire safety requirements. When the Wanxin Building was designed and constructed, the Interim Provisions had not yet been issued. Although there were no mandatory national standards for external wall insulation building materials at that time, Wanxin Company, as an enterprise specializing in real estate development, should have mastered the basic fire performance of building materials. Before the completion acceptance of the Wanxin Building, the Interim Provisions were issued, and the state stipulated mandatory standards for insulation building materials on external walls of civil buildings. At this time, Wanxin Company should have known that the building materials involved did not comply with national mandatory standards and that, compared with national standards, there were safety hazards in the external insulation layer of the Wanxin Building. However, Wanxin Company did not take reasonable and appropriate remedial measures to reduce fire hazards, such as partially replacing flame-retardant materials on platforms or low-rise areas that might be affected by fireworks, or setting up fire isolation belts on mid-to-high floors. In summary, Wanxin Company's use of building materials without fire performance objectively increased the building's fire safety hazards, directly endangering the public safety of the building and certain areas nearby. As the construction unit, Wanxin Company failed to fulfill its duty of care and was clearly at fault. The original trial's finding that Wanxin Company was not at fault for the occurrence of the fire accident was erroneous and should be corrected. Second, Wanxin Company and Zhao Shuhua established a commercial housing sales contract relationship for the purchase of the house involved. As the developer and seller of the house involved, Wanxin Company was obliged to deliver a commercial house of qualified quality. Considering the特殊性 of the subject matter of the commercial housing sales contract, that is, the house, the buyer generally cannot inspect whether the purchased house complies with fire safety regulations, which building materials used in the construction are flammable, which are flame-retardant, and whether there are fire safety hazards. It is difficult to apply the rule that the buyer should inspect the product quality in a timely manner after delivery of the subject matter under a general goods sales contract. Article 17 of the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" signed between Zhao Shuhua and Wanxin Company stipulated that the right to use the outer wall of the building where the commercial house involved was located belonged to Wanxin Company. As the user of the outer wall of the Wanxin Building, Wanxin Company bore the obligation to manage and maintain the outer wall of the Wanxin Building. As a homebuyer, Zhao Shuhua used the purchased property normally and was not at fault. The seller, Wanxin Company, directly caused the fire to spread and cause disaster due to faults such as fire protection defects in the building materials of the Wanxin Building and improper laying of ignitable materials, resulting in property damage to Zhao Shuhua. There is a causal relationship between Wanxin Company's fault and Zhao Shuhua's loss. Wanxin Company should bear compensation liability according to its fault and shall not be exempted from liability due to reasons such as the Wanxin Building passing completion acceptance, the fire protection subcontract having been approved, or the national standard for the external insulation layer being issued later.

In summary, Wanxin Company, as the construction party, developer, and external wall user of the Wanxin Building, is the main body responsible for the fire safety of the Wanxin Building. Wanxin Company failed to fulfill its duty of care for fire safety, did not take remedial measures to eliminate fire hazards, and delivered the house to the homebuyer Zhao Shuhua. Its fault was obvious. The first and second instance judgments that Wanxin Company was not at fault lacked factual and legal basis. Wanxin Company infringed upon Zhao Shuhua's civil rights and interests due to its fault and shall bear tort liability according to law.

(2) Zhongyi Company shall bear tort liability

On August 26, 2007, Article 46, Paragraph 1 of the "Property Management Regulations" revised by the State Council stipulated, "For acts within the property management area that violate laws and regulations on public security, environmental protection, property decoration and use, etc., the property service enterprise shall stop them and promptly report to the relevant administrative departments." Article 47, Paragraph 1 stipulated, "The property service enterprise shall assist in doing a good job of safety precautions within the property management area. When a safety accident occurs, the property service enterprise, while taking emergency measures, shall promptly report to the relevant administrative departments and assist in rescue work." Article 21 of the "Interim Convention for Owners of Huangchao Wanxin International Tower (Apartment)," which has the nature of a property service contract, stipulated that when there is a safety hazard in the Wanxin Building property that endangers the public interest or the legitimate rights and interests of other owners, Zhongyi Company shall promptly take measures to eliminate the hazard. It can be seen that one of the purposes for owners to sign a property service contract is to obtain basic protection for their personal and property safety. Accordingly, property service enterprises, in accordance with the above regulations and property service contracts, have the obligation to do a good job of corresponding safety precautions within the property management area and shall assist in preventing, stopping, or rescuing accidents or hazards that may endanger the personal or property safety of specific or non-specific persons such as owners and hotel guests. In this case, Zhongyi Company did not fulfill its statutory or contractual safety precaution obligations. First, Zhongyi Company failed to fulfill its duty of care. When questioned by this Court, Zhongyi Company acknowledged that, as the preliminary property service enterprise for the Wanxin Building, it began to perform property service duties when Wanxin Company transferred the completion acceptance procedures of the Wanxin Building to Zhongyi Company. Zhongyi Company was aware that the external wall insulation building materials of the Wanxin Building were combustible and did not have fire performance. Knowing that the Wanxin Building had fire safety hazards, Zhongyi Company should have been more meticulous and careful in performing its property safety precaution duties, but it subjectively failed to fulfill the duty of care of a professional manager. Second, Zhongyi Company had the ability to prevent and control the dangerous act of setting off fireworks by a third party. The criminal judgment in the Li Xin arson case, based on the contents recorded in the "Fire Scene Investigation Record," determined that the location where the third party set off the combination fireworks was at the southwest corner of the outdoor parking lot on the south side of Block B of the Wanxin Building (10.8 meters from the south wall of Block B, and 16 meters from the southwest corner of the wall, there was a firework remnant, and 2.2 meters to the east of that remnant was another remnant). It can be determined that the location where the fireworks involved were set off was in the parking lot on the south side of the Wanxin Building, adjacent to the large LED screen on the south side of the Wanxin Building and the high-level platform. The above locations where the fireworks were set off and the fire occurred were within the visual range of Zhongyi Company's monitoring or patrols, but Zhongyi Company did not take appropriate measures to discover the fire or prevent the disaster. Zhongyi Company argued that the above location was not within the scope of property management, and the owner check-in documents it submitted had unclear provisions on the scope of property management. When questioned by this Court, Zhongyi Company acknowledged that part of the outdoor parking lot involved was managed by it. This Court holds that, under the circumstances where the property service contract has unclear provisions on the scope of the property service area and the Wanxin Building is not enclosed, in accordance with Articles 61 and 62 of the Contract Law of the PRC, the scope of the property service area shall be determined based on the reasonable area that can achieve the purpose of concluding the property service contract, i.e., to ensure the personal and property safety of owners. Accordingly, the existing evidence cannot exclude that the location where the fireworks involved were set off was not within Zhongyi Company's property management scope. Third, Zhongyi Company failed to fulfill its special duty of property security during the Spring Festival period. Setting off fireworks and firecrackers on New Year's Eve is a traditional Chinese custom. Zhongyi Company did not provide evidence to prove that it took fire prevention measures that could effectively prevent the occurrence of fire and eliminate accident hazards at this high-risk time point for fires, such as strengthening patrols, timely monitoring, and preparing sufficient fire extinguishing equipment. It failed to discover that guests staying at the Wanxin Building were setting off fireworks in close proximity around the Wanxin Building. In addition, based on the existing evidence, it cannot be determined that the sprinkler system in the house involved was operating normally at the time of the fire. The division of responsibilities between Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company regarding the management and maintenance of fire protection facilities and equipment was unclear, and it should also be presumed that Zhongyi Company had management responsibilities for the maintenance of fire protection facilities. In summary, considering that the fire occurred in the outdoor parking lot of the Wanxin Building, that the area around the Wanxin Building is an open block where the property's own area is not clearly demarcated from the municipal public area, and that there is an关联 relationship between Zhongyi Company's failure to properly perform its property safety precaution duties and the occurrence of the fire, Zhongyi Company shall bear corresponding civil liability for tort compensation. Zhongyi Company's defense that the location where the third party set off the fireworks was not within its property management scope and thus it should not bear liability cannot be established.

In this case, compared with Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company, Zhao Shuhua was not at fault for the occurrence of the fire. The first and second instance judgments holding that Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company did not bear tort compensation liability would mean that the innocent victim bears the property losses caused by the fire triggered by others' negligence, which violates the principle of fault in tort law. The original judgment was unbalanced in substance, and this Court corrects it.

II. How should the liability of Zhongyi Company and Wanxin Company be determined

The effective criminal judgment and the fire accident determination report involved in the case determined that the third party's setting off fireworks constituted the crime of arson, which was the main cause of the fire at the Wanxin Building. Wanxin Company laying flammable materials that ignited the external wall building materials, which then formed a three-dimensional combustion, leading to the expansion and spread of the fire, was the process of loss occurrence. That is, the fire in this case was the result of multiple causes leading to one consequence; the tortious acts and causative factors were sequential rather than cumulative. Each party involved had significant negligence regarding the occurrence of the fire, but none intentionally sought the harmful consequences. Wanxin Company's fault was also insufficient to cause all the losses, so it should not bear compensation liability for all the victim's losses. After all, Wanxin Company did not actively act to infringe upon Zhao Shuhua's rights and interests, nor should it bear the primary responsibility. Zhongyi Company did not fulfill its duty in property safety precautions, had management omissions, and was at fault, but its conduct did not directly cause the fire. Since the tort by Wanxin Company and others infringed upon Zhao Shuhua's civil rights and interests, Wanxin Company and others shall first bear compensation liability, and Zhongyi Company shall bear corresponding supplementary liability within the scope it could foresee and prevent.

In summary, the tortfeasors involved in this case did not have common intent or common negligence. Instead, several acts of each party at different times were closely combined to cause the fire, thereby causing losses to Zhao Shuhua. Article 12 of the Tort Liability Law stipulates that where two or more persons each commit a tortious act, causing the same damage, if the degree of liability can be determined, they shall each bear corresponding liability. Therefore, this Court determines that Wanxin Company shall bear 40% of the compensation liability for Zhao Shuhua's losses, and Zhongyi Company shall bear supplementary liability within the scope of no more than 30% of Zhao Shuhua's total losses.

III. How should the scope of Zhao Shuhua's property losses be determined

According to Zhao Shuhua's claims in the first instance, the scope of property losses she asserted included: 1. House loss of RMB 4,573,155; 2. Interior property loss of RMB 2,199,363; 3. Rental expenses of RMB 187,400; 4. Deed tax of RMB 182,926.20 paid for house purchase, maintenance fund of RMB 8,646.56, and house registration filing fee of RMB 5,000; 5. Appreciation loss of the property of RMB 2,500,625; 6. Overdue interest on the bank loan for the property involved of RMB 100,000 and liquidated damages of RMB 228,000; 7. The insurance claim payment received by Wanxin Company from the insurance company. During the retrial, Zhao Shuhua adjusted the amount of loss compensation: she no longer claimed the appreciation loss of the house, the house loss was reduced to RMB 3,186,300, and the rental loss was increased to RMB 357,000. This Court hears the case within the scope of her amended claim not exceeding the scope of the first instance claim.

1.  Regarding the house loss, interest, liquidated damages, and related taxes and fees. Because Zhao Shuhua was delinquent on the bank loan for the house involved, Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. filed another lawsuit to claim the creditor's rights. The house involved was sold through enforcement auction, and Zhao Shuhua has lost ownership. The house price, loan interest, liquidated damages, and related taxes and fees arose from Zhao Shuhua's failure to fulfill repayment obligations in the loan legal relationship, which pertains to solvency and does not have a direct causal relationship with the fire. Zhao Shuhua's assertion of this part of the loss lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported.

2.  Regarding the part of the insurance claim payment received by Wanxin Company. According to the contents of the "Survey Report" involved in the case, the insured parties under the policies involved were all Wanxin Company, and the subject matter of the relevant policies was the buildings at No. 392 and No. 390A Qingnian Street, Heping District, and the ancillary equipment of the buildings. Zhao Shuhua's assertion of loss from the insurance claim payment lacks sufficient basis and is not supported.

3.  Regarding the rental loss part. The parties in this case do not dispute that the house involved was uninhabitable after being burned down, and that Wanxin Company subsequently carried out overall restoration of the burned house. Therefore, the rent incurred by Zhao Shuhua for renting another place to live from the time of the fire until the completion of the restoration of the house involved by Wanxin Company is a loss caused by the inability to use the house involved due to the fire and should be supported. The Shenyang Fire Bureau's "Opinion on the Fire Protection Acceptance of the Partial Decoration and Renovation Project of Block B of Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Building" (Shen Gong Xiao Yan [2013] No. 0050) stated that Block B of the Wanxin Building was redecorated and passed the fire acceptance on February 25, 2013. During the retrial, Wanxin Company claimed that the apartments in Block B of the Wanxin Building were redecorated no later than March 4, 2013. In addition, combined with the "House Rental Agreement" signed by Zhao Shuhua and a third party (rent of RMB 36,000 from February 13, 2011, to February 12, 2012; rent of RMB 64,800 from February 13, 2012, to February 12, 2013; rent of RMB 10,800 from February 13, 2013, to April 12, 2013), based on the above evidence, it can be determined that the total reasonable rental period from the occurrence of the fire to the completion of the redecorations of Block B of the Wanxin Building to habitable standard was RMB 111,600, which should be included in Zhao Shuhua's property loss.

4.  Regarding the interior property loss part. In the original trial, Zhao Shuhua submitted comparison photos of the house involved before and after the fire, as well as written evidence such as statements from a certain housing agency and its employees, which can prove that before the fire, the house involved contained relatively complete household belongings such as furniture, appliances, clothing, and jewelry. It is common sense for a residential house to store such household property. Although Wanxin Company and Zhongyi Company did not acknowledge the above property, they failed to provide a reasonable explanation. Based on the detailed list of interior property provided by Zhao Shuhua, combined with factors such as local living habits, the time of purchase of the items, the depreciation of the items due to use, and the victim's living standard, this Court determines that the amount of Zhao Shuhua's interior property loss shall be 80% of the amount she claimed, i.e., RMB 1,759,490.4 (RMB 2,199,363 × 80%).

Zhao Shuhua's property loss shall be determined as RMB 1,871,090.4 (rental loss of RMB 111,600 + interior property loss of RMB 1,759,490.4). Wanxin Company shall compensate Zhao Shuhua for the loss of RMB 748,436.16 (RMB 1,871,090.4 × 40%), and Zhongyi Company shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of a loss of RMB 561,327.12 (RMB 1,871,090.4 × 30%).

In summary, Zhao Shuhua's grounds for retrial are partially established, and this Court supports them. In accordance with Article 2, Article 6, and Article 12 of the Tort Liability Law of the PRC, Article 207, Paragraph 1 and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 407 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1.  Set aside the Civil Judgment (2013) Shen Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province and the Civil Judgment (2015) Liao Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 00300 of the Liaoning High People's Court;

2.  Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. shall compensate Zhao Shuhua for the loss of RMB 748,436.16 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect;

3.  Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd. shall bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of a loss amount of RMB 561,327.12;

4.  Dismiss Zhao Shuhua's other claims.

If the monetary payment obligation is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 79,400 for the first instance shall be borne by Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 45,000, by Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 29,000, and by Zhao Shuhua in the amount of RMB 5,400; Court acceptance fee of RMB 81,696 for the second instance shall be borne by Shenyang Huangchao Wanxin Hotel Management Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 45,000, by Shenyang Zhongyi Wanxin Property Management Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 31,000, and by Zhao Shuhua in the amount of RMB 5,696.
